ip-author.detail: No dedicated FTO page or mention was found.

powerpatent.detail: Offered as an attorney-guided service combining software with human experts, plus educational content, but no confirmed self-serve dedicated FTO product page.

cypris.detail: The IP solutions page dedicates a section to FTO with "automated reporting for prior art, FTO, and landscape analysis," and an embedded case study shows Cypris generating per-patent FTO risk ratings.

patlytics.detail: Search and claim-charting tools are usable for IPR petition prep today; a dedicated PTAB-specific workflow is not yet a named product module.

solve-intelligence.detail: Offers invalidity chart generation and general litigation support, but no page names a dedicated IPR/PTAB workflow specifically.

patsnap.detail: Claim-chart data is marketed as usable for IPR and infringement analysis, and Eureka publishes PTAB commentary, but there's no dedicated named IPR/PTAB litigation workflow product.

iprally.detail: A dedicated "Patent Invalidity Search" use case finds invalidating art for specific publications to challenge chosen claims, directly relevant to building an IPR petition, but it produces search results rather than a chart and no page names a dedicated IPR/PTAB workflow.

clarivate-innography.detail: Darts-ip is positioned as global litigation case-law search with "claim construction search" and a "find the killer argument" tool, and Clarivate separately offers a distinct patent (in)validity search service, but no page explicitly frames these as IPR/PTAB-specific.

anaqua.detail: Unified Patents (acquired Aug 2026) runs a dedicated PTAB docket portal and an AI claim-charting tool for invalidity, but per Anaqua's own materials Unified operates independently post-acquisition, so this isn't yet confirmed as delivered to Anaqua's own customers.

lexisnexis-ip.detail: PTAB Argument Finder targets ex parte prosecution appeals rather than IPR invalidity charting; a separate "Disputes" dataset covers PTAB case data as litigation analytics, not an active charting/drafting workflow.

cipher.detail: Not mentioned on Cipher's product page; litigation/PTAB dispute data appears to live in a separate LexisNexis "Disputes" product.

juristat.detail: Offers a "PTAB Expert Search" tool to find expert witnesses for IPR/CBM/PGR cases, which is real but is expert-recruiting rather than invalidity search/charting.

patent-bots.detail: Examiner Stats covers ex parte appeal/PTAB outcome statistics tied to prosecution, not a dedicated IPR/PTAB invalidity search-and-chart workflow.

alt-legal.detail: Not mentioned; Alt Legal is explicitly a docketing/deadline platform, primarily trademark-focused with patent docketing as an add-on.

pqai.detail: No litigation or PTAB feature was found. PQAI is a free, open-source nonprofit research project rather than a commercial vendor, so its scope is intentionally narrow.

ip-copilot.detail: Not mentioned anywhere on the site; no IPR, PTAB, or litigation-support capability is described.

harvey.detail: Harvey assists teams in preparing draft sections of PGR and IPR briefs by synthesizing statutory provisions, key precedents, and technical records -- the same configurable-workflow-with-human-review standard that earns Harvey a yes on claim-charting, prior-art-search, and office-action-response.

legora.detail: Not mentioned anywhere; an independent review confirms Legora's practice areas exclude IP.

spellbook.detail: Not offered; Spellbook's IP-related function is limited to drafting and reviewing IP licensing and ownership contract clauses.

robin-ai.detail: Robin AI is confirmed fully dismantled: it failed to close a funding round in late 2025, laid off roughly a third of staff, was listed for distressed sale, had its managed-services arm acquired by Scissero in Dec 2025, and had its engineering team absorbed by Microsoft in early 2026. It was always a commercial contract-review platform with no patent-specific capability, and no live product remains to possess one.

leya.detail: Leya rebranded to Legora in February 2025 (confirmed still accurate). Legora's own site and independent vendor profiles describe it purely as a general legal-AI workspace for M&A, Litigation, Banking, Tax, and Insurance, with no patent/IP vertical or dedicated module found anywhere in its marketing.

cocounsel.detail: No dedicated PTAB or IPR workflow was found; searches return only generic PTAB background information, nothing product-specific.

ironclad.detail: Direct searches for Ironclad plus patent/IP or PTAB turned up no results tying it to any patent-litigation workflow.

linksquares.detail: The same searches returned no evidence of any patent-litigation feature.

draftwise.detail: Not found; searches returned only generic patent-prosecution background, no DraftWise-specific results.

genie-ai.detail: Not found; the same searches returned no company-specific hits.

ktmine.detail: The Patents Search App includes a dedicated "PTAB Trials" field listing all PTAB trials for a given patent, but there's no dedicated IPR/PTAB litigation-support workflow beyond that listing.

ipwe.detail: No mention found in press coverage or search snippets, and the company's own site could not be reached directly to confirm either way.

deepip.detail: Invalidity Search's own FAQ states it helps professionals "weaken or invalidate patents during disputes, PTAB proceedings, or licensing negotiations," generating sourced invalidity claim charts -- the core technical work product of an IPR petition.

junior.detail: Universe's Litigation Support section maps patent families against targets, analyzes prior art, and builds structured claim charts for validity challenges, but no page names PTAB or IPR specifically.

ankar-ai.detail: The Claim Charts product explicitly states its charts are used "across prosecution, litigation and post-grant proceedings" to map prior art against asserted claims and identify vulnerable claims -- genuine post-grant work product.

patented-ai.detail: The site explicitly markets "court-proven, IPR-grade source code analysis to invalidate patents" under its litigation section.

xlscout.detail: The Invalidator LLM explicitly assesses IPR vulnerability and produces invalidity summaries positioned as inputs for IPR petitions or defense.

nlpatent.detail: The live product page now lists "Validity/Invalidity" ("challenge or defend a granted patent... pressure testing the issued claims against the art") as a current workflow, shipped since the company's rebrand -- a genuine invalidity capability, though the page never names PTAB or IPR explicitly.

patentpal.detail: No evidence found in any source searched. The company's main site blocked direct fetching, so this row relies on third-party reviews and cached subpages rather than the vendor's own copy.

amplified-ai.detail: The company published benchmarking of its retrieval against PTAB IPR-challenged patents showing IPR relevance, but no named PTAB/IPR module was found — it appears folded into general invalidity search.

iprova.detail: No PTAB, IPR, or invalidity content exists anywhere in Iprova's public materials; its tools stop at invention creation and documentation.

minesoft.detail: Invalidity Screening produces genuine invalidity work product (claim-by-claim invalidity chart, ranked prior art, invalidity arguments) framed for deciding whether to challenge a third-party patent, but it never names PTAB or IPR specifically.

questel.detail: Prosecution Pack provides PTAB final-decision win/loss statistics by examiner, law firm, and applicant for ex parte prosecution appeals -- backward-looking statistics, not a generator of IPR-specific litigation work product.

park-ip.detail: Its litigation page confirms services are translation, interpreting, and e-discovery only, not substantive IPR/PTAB analysis.

patseer.detail: General invalidity-search tooling applies to IPR prep, but no page names a dedicated PTAB/IPR workflow specifically.

patently.detail: The "Shape" module supports prosecution, oppositions, and litigation workflows generally, but no page names IPR or PTAB specifically.

ip-author.detail: No dedicated PTAB or IPR page or mention was found.

powerpatent.detail: No evidence found; the product is founder/startup-focused drafting and prosecution, not litigation.

cypris.detail: No PTAB, IPR, or litigation feature was found anywhere on cypris.ai, including the MCP integration page; a previously-cited claim about API access to raw PTAB data could not be re-confirmed this session.

office-action-response.author: Jonah P., Patent Agent, Small-Business
office-action-response.text: Solve Intelligence takes in unstructured data such as public prior art, internal specifications, inventors' notes, and drawings... Solve takes in office actions, parses them, and gives immediate comparison between claims, rejections, and examiner's reasoning... Solve does 20+ hours of application drafting work and 5+ hours of office action handling work each in less than 1 hour.

office-action-response.author: Rohan W., Small-Business
office-action-response.text: On the prosecution side, it really gets to the point of the examiner's objections and helps in devising a way past them.

prior-art-search.author: Rohan W., Small-Business
prior-art-search.text: ...a tool to identify differences from prior art and potential inventive step issues could also be beneficial. (Listed by the reviewer as a missing capability they'd like to see.)

portfolio-analytics.author: Astrid Bakker
portfolio-analytics.text: PatSnap provides an excellent patent search functionality with visual and analytical overviews of IP portfolios.

portfolio-analytics.author: Chih-Yuan T., Head of Computational Group, Pharmaceuticals
portfolio-analytics.text: ...their proprietary analysis module that can map out the landscape of industrials that have patents relevant to the queries.

portfolio-analytics.author: Connie S., Paralegal, Medical Devices
portfolio-analytics.text: Setting up customized searches/reports and information for looking at various IP landscapes of competitors.

prior-art-search.author: Patrick A., IP Analyst, Information Services
prior-art-search.text: Quick Invalidity and Novelty Reports & easy to use Patent Categorizer (AI based Taxonomy). Amazing experience with 24/7 customer support. (Cons: limitations in creating Taxonomy should be improved.)

prior-art-search.author: Ritesh M., Senior IP Scientist / Patent Portfolio Mgmt Lead, Chemicals
prior-art-search.text: Mostly using this software for patent searches related to patentability, invalidity and FTO. Also for patent analytics. Ease of use, user friendly, great patent coverage, highlighting options, great analytics options. (Cons: limited export options beyond 1000 records, occasionally slow.)

portfolio-analytics.author: Ritesh M., Senior IP Scientist / Patent Portfolio Mgmt Lead, Chemicals
portfolio-analytics.text: Mostly using this software for patent searches related to patentability, invalidity and FTO. Also for patent analytics. Ease of use, user friendly, great patent coverage, highlighting options, great analytics options. (Cons: limited export options beyond 1000 records, occasionally slow.)

portfolio-analytics.author: Géraldine L., Competitive Intelligence Officer, Farming
portfolio-analytics.text: I have a good experience. The database is complete, data is quickly found. The different charts and visualization options are really a plus. The accuracy of the information (statuses, families) and ease of data access stand out.

fto-analysis.author: Ritesh M., Senior IP Scientist / Patent Portfolio Mgmt Lead, Chemicals
fto-analysis.text: Mostly using this software for patent searches related to patentability, invalidity and FTO. Also for patent analytics. Ease of use, user friendly, great patent coverage, highlighting options, great analytics options. (Cons: limited export options beyond 1000 records, occasionally slow.)

portfolio-analytics.author: William D., Partner, Law Practice (Mid-Market)
portfolio-analytics.text: User-friendly platform providing invaluable information for firm marketing efforts. The ability to filter results in several areas, including filing and disposition date as well as art unit, is really helpful in evaluating performance metrics. Quick and accurate compilation and display of prosecution results.

portfolio-analytics.author: Marcy S., Founding Partner, Law Practice
portfolio-analytics.text: Alt Legal is the most intuitive IP software I have used in my decade of IP experience at both big and small firms. The Alt Legal team is extremely responsive... the reporting functions are exceptional for sharing portfolio status reports with clients.

fto-analysis.author: Alexander G., Patent Searcher, Legal Services
fto-analysis.text: The system includes work flow tools which allow effective processing of the most demanding projects like complex FTOs or advanced portfolio analysis.

portfolio-analytics.author: Alexander G., Patent Searcher, Legal Services
portfolio-analytics.text: Statistics, AI and traditional searching are well integrated in a single package.

portfolio-analytics.author: Lisa D., Associate Director Patent Search & Analytics, Biotechnology
portfolio-analytics.text: While the analytics section was good, the graphs produced were not the best and data had to be downloaded to another visualization software for presentations.

prior-art-search.author: Carlo S., CFO and Head of IP
prior-art-search.text: I look for prior art to manage both new patent filing or to look for potential invalidation in the context of patent litigations.

fto-analysis.author: Joshua Dalby
fto-analysis.text: Great, intuitive and efficient tool -- used for freedom-to-operate searches as part of my regular workflow.

prior-art-search.author: Carl
prior-art-search.text: AI powered vector search -- part of my daily prior-art and portfolio document review.

prior-art-search.author: Jon Hauser
prior-art-search.text: Vector Search allows free-form text searching... completely blows old fashioned keyword/abstract searching out of the water.

prior-art-search.author: Luke
prior-art-search.text: A Game-Changer in Patent Searching -- described in the context of novelty-search/FTO workflow.

prior-art-search.author: Charlie, European patent attorney
prior-art-search.text: Precisely where and how we've identified certain patents -- used daily for prior-art search.

portfolio-analytics.author: Stephen Scott
portfolio-analytics.text: I was able to use C-Tree to visualise the entire portfolio in an instant, and gain an understanding of the family structure.

office-action-response.author: Tom
office-action-response.text: Patently's Shape (prosecution) and Create (drafting) are exceptional. The chat function is a powerful tool that helps me rapidly improve drafts and responses.

prior-art-search.author: John Miller, Global Intellectual Property Leader, Chevron Oronite
prior-art-search.text: What used to take days of manual prior art searching can now be done in minutes. IP Author identifies highly relevant references quickly and transparently, helping us reach patentability decisions faster and with confidence.

office-action-response.author: David Chen, Esq., IP Partner, West Coast IP Law
office-action-response.text: OfficeAction AI has cut my Office Action response time in half. The AI-generated arguments are impressively on-point, and I can focus more on strategy rather than routine drafting.

office-action-response.author: Michael Rodriguez, Managing Partner, Innovation Legal Group
office-action-response.text: Our firm has seen a 40% reduction in time spent on Office Action responses. The collaboration features make it easy for partners to review associate work, and clients love the faster turnaround times.
